Subject: Renewal conversation and usage files

Jasmine,

Quick note ahead of next week's renewal checkpoint — CrescentPay is looking to consolidate spend and evaluate a shift from hosted on-demand to a reserved (dedicated) pool for inference. I've attached our last 12 months of token usage (CSV) and a short summary of peak-day profiles.

Primary asks:
- What does a committed reserved capacity proposal look like for our current profile (average 6M tokens/day, 3x peaks)?
- Rough ROI: how long to break even vs hosted on-demand?
- Any performance improvements (latency/throughput) we should expect?

Can you send a short readout we can share with our procurement team ahead of the call?

Thanks — if easier, cc procurement@crescentpay.com and I'll loop in our finance lead.

Alex
Head of Platform — CrescentPay

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation and usage files

Alex — thanks for the data, and sorry for the slight delay. I've pulled a short readout with modeled cost scenarios and expected performance delta if CrescentPay moves to a Reserved (Dedicated) capacity commitment. See summary below and attached two files (perf_report_q1.pdf, savings_model_v2.xlsx).

Executive summary (high level)
- Current 12-month spend (hosted on-demand): ~$2.1M total; average effective cost ≈ $0.023 per 1k tokens (we used your supplied mix of embeddings + chat tokens).
- Proposed reserved capacity (3x baseline with burst lane): estimated committed monthly spend ≈ $97k (annualized ≈ $1.16M).
- Modeled on-demand vs reserved delta: ~44% unit cost reduction on steady-state traffic; net savings over 12 months ≈ $940k before credits and overage policies.
- Break-even (cumulative): ~7–9 months depending on peak smoothing and KV-cache hit rates.

Performance and reliability notes
- p95 generation latency improved by ~28% in our internal pilots for similar models running on a dedicated pool (reduced queueing and prioritized KV cache locality).
- Throughput: sustained concurrent streams increased ~2.2x in our tests with the same GPU footprint due to continuous batching optimizations.

Operational / contract considerations
- We recommend a base commitment at 3x current baseline with a 20% burst credit pool for peak-day elasticity. This preserves SLAs and avoids frequent throttling.
- Optional add-on: 2-week surge buffer for the first quarter to account for forecast variance (one-time credit).
- Standard SLO: 99.5% availability for dedicated tenants; p95 latency target vs current baseline will be included in the SOW.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Internal ops sizing confirmation (Ben) — confirm the 3x baseline and burst % is operationally sound.
2) Legal/Procurement draft (Monica) — prepare a short SOW + amendment and DocuSign-ready commitment.
3) I will pull a line-item cost sheet and final proposal to share with Procurement this week.

I attached the performance readout (perf_report_q1.pdf) and the savings model I used (savings_model_v2.xlsx). If you want a tighter sensitivity (e.g., different cache-hit assumptions), I can run that quickly.

--
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Southern Region
Redwood Inference
